text:
Mira (support): Customer (payflow-inc) reporting a surge of 504s and 5xxs from hosted API yesterday evening. They see long tail timeouts (~30s) on generation routes and a pileup in our request queue. Logs attached: `queue_depth=4096 batcher_backlog=78 continuous_batch_queue=high` — can we triage?

Jorge (eng-sre): Thanks — putting this on high priority. Which tenant, region? Any recent deploys or model swaps?

Mira (support): Tenant payflow-prod in us-west-2. They reported the errors starting ~19:12 PDT after a big traffic spike. No model change on their side; we had a routine runtime push at 19:05 (small allocator tweak). Customer included a curl example that consistently times out: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" -d '{"input":"summarize..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` -> hangs then 504.

Sylvia (eng-runtime): Seeing the same graph in runtime telemetry: continuous-batcher backlog growing, dequeue rate plateaus. Kernel-level traces show many inflight KV cache misses and long per-token stalls. Sample snippet from the collector: `router.request_queue_depth{region="us-west-2"} 3987` and `batcher.pending_batches 62`. Looks like queue depth exceeded the soft-threshold and requests are queuing up behind cold KV loads.

infra-bot: Deploy `runtime/allocator` rolled at 2024-09-17T19:05:12Z by deploy-bot (sha: a1b2c3). Autoscale metrics show no extra workers spun up until 19:20.

Dan (oncall): Can we reproduce quickly? If this is continuous-batcher backlog + cold KV, immediate mitigation options: 1) lower MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH for hosted region, 2) enable emergency prefix caching for that tenant, 3) force additional worker spin-up. I can apply a throttle if someone gives the green light.

Mira (support): Customer wants a fix asap. Granting permission to throttle for payflow-prod.

Jorge (eng-sre): Running a small config change: set tenant_throttle(payflow-prod)=0.6 and reduce global max_request_queue=1024 in us-west-2. Command I pushed: `kubectl -n runtime set env deployment/router MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH=1024 --record` — will monitor.

Sylvia (eng-runtime): Also enabling emergency KV warm cache for top prefixes for that tenant: `runtime-cli kvcache warm --tenant=payflow-prod --prefixes=summary,invoice` — warming in progress.

Dan (oncall): After throttle + queue reduction + warming: p95 dropped from 18.6s -> 1.2s in ~2m, queue depth down to ~300. Customer confirmed latency improving (:thumbsup:). Marking immediate mitigation successful.

Mira (support): Customer confirms all calls healthy now. They sent logs showing retry storms subsiding.

Jorge (eng-sre): Postmortem items: 1) investigate the allocator change at 19:05 that delayed autoscale, 2) add an early alarm for batcher.pending_batches > 40, 3) add tenant-level circuit-breaker default for heavy-tail tenants. Will open follow-up tickets.

Sylvia (eng-runtime): Added a quick tracing span to detect KV cold-miss amplification in batchers. We'll correlate with recent kernel change.

Dan (oncall): Summary: Sev2 (customer-facing latency/5xx). Mitigated via throttle + queue depth reduction + KV warm. Owner: eng-runtime + eng-sre. Follow-up boarding: retrospective scheduled tomorrow.

Mira (support): Closing the support escalation with the customer and sharing mitigation notes. Thanks team.
